text:
lina (support): noticed a surge in latency tickets starting ~03:12 UTC. multiple customers reporting p95/p99 spikes after the runtime rollout around 03:05. grafana panel: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd/infra-latency?orgId=1 (p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms, p99 ~1.2s)

mia (SRE): pulling it up. which rollout ID? any canary notes?

deploy-bot: Canary rollout complete: runtime-service v2.14.0 -> 100% on cluster-ai-prod at 03:05 UTC (initiated 02:50 UTC).

lina (support): yes v2.14.0. Support see some 429s + timeouts too but main complaint is tail latency.

jurgen (runtime): I pushed batching heuristics change + new kv-cache eviction in v2.14.0. Could be the batching window increase (default 10ms -> 25ms) to improve throughput.

omar (eng): seeing traces — span waterfall shows queueing on inference worker pre-dispatch. The request enters, spends ~200-400ms in local dispatcher waiting for batch formation. GPU execution time hasn't changed much.

mia (SRE): ok that aligns with p95 spike. is it across all model routes or a subset?

lina (support): mostly chat endpoints and larger context requests (>1k tokens). embeddings routes flat.

omar (eng): hypothesis: the increased batch window caused longer waiters when traffic is bursty, raising p95/p99. For long-context requests, assembly cost + longer wait leads to compounding.

ella (prod-ops): any immediate mitigations we can flip? rollback canary? partial config override?

jurgen (runtime): we can patch the runtime config at the routing layer to lower batch window for chat routes. quick rollback to v2.13.9 is also possible but will require rolling back ephemeral fixes (kv-cache).

mia (SRE): let's do a two-pronged plan: 1) quick config override to reduce batch window on high-latency routes 2) if that doesn't help, rollback to 2.13.9. I'll run the config patch now.

mia (SRE): applying patch to route policy for service 'chat' and 'chat-longctx':
```
PATCH /api/routing/policies/override
{
  "routes": ["/v1/chat","/v1/chat/longctx"],
  "batch_window_ms": 6
}
```

mia (SRE): pushed, propagation in progress. waiting 30s to see new metrics.

kevin (cs): customers on premium tier are asking for ETA — I told them we're investigating and applying mitigations. they want status updates every 15m.

omar (eng): while we wait, I'll run a quick A/B repro against v2.14.0 with synthetic burst traffic to confirm behavior. sharing load test script: 
```
node load.js --rps 200 --burst=10 --ctx=1500 --url https://api.redwood/v1/chat
```

omar (eng): repro shows median ~130ms, p95 ~430ms on v2.14.0; same test against a local v2.13.9 instance yields p95 ~110ms.

mia (SRE): grafana shows p95 starting to trend down after config push, from 420ms -> 160ms in ~3m. p99 still has a few stragglers but much improved.

lina (support): tickets updated, customers notified. :thumbsup:

jurgen (runtime): good. we should still roll back the batching param default in v2.14.1 and re-evaluate the kv-cache change separately. The kv-cache saw a small increase in eviction churn that could amplify latency on long-context requests.

ella (prod-ops): do we want a formal rollback now or a targeted revert of batching defaults?

mia (SRE): since quick config fix worked, set the action: revert default batching window change in code (prepare v2.14.1 patch) + add a canary specifically for latency-sensitive routes. no full rollback needed.

omar (eng): I'll open PR to revert default batch window and add feature flag: `runtime.batch_window_ms` per-route override + integration test. linking PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4723

jurgen (runtime): I'll add perf unit tests to catch p95 regressions in the CI canary job. Also increasing canary monitoring sensitivity for p95/p99.

mia (SRE): follow-ups: 1) postmortem with timeline + customer impact 2) add automated bisection job that runs before 100% rollout for perf-sensitive flags 3) run throughload/perf suite on canary nodes 4) update runbook with explicit steps for batch-window misconfig/rollback.

kevin (cs): please cc me on postmortem; I'll coordinate customer comms.

lina (support): closing thread for now, monitoring. will reopen if anything pops. thanks everyone.

-- notes/observations --
- root cause: change to batching heuristics (increase in default batch window) combined with increased eviction churn in kv-cache impacting long-context request assembly -> increased pre-dispatch queueing -> p95/p99 regression.
- short-term mitigation: per-route config override (lowered batch_window_ms to 6) pushed at 03:28 UTC -> p95 reduced dramatically within 3 minutes.
- medium-term: revert default, feature-flag the new behavior, add more perf canaries targeted at tail latency, expand CI perf tests.
- commands used: rollback (if needed): `deployctl rollback runtime-service --to v2.13.9` ; config override REST PATCH (see above) ; repro script (see above).

action items: [omar] open PR to revert default + feature flag; [jurgen] add perf tests & canary checks; [mia] update runbook and run perf canaries before next rollout; [kevin] coordinate customer comms; [lina] assemble ticket list for affected customers.

thread resolved: temporary mitigation applied, monitoring ongoing.
